title: Fix Modification-Scope Enforcement in EDD Refinement

story.so_that: we reduce workflow-source corruption incidents and avoid manual worktree cleanup, keeping EDD refinement runs recoverable within the existing SLO
story.i_want: the EDD refinement workflow to reject any file change outside the authorized modification scope and leave the repository clean

journey.before: EDD refinement runs can drift out of scope and modify the workflow's own source without detection or cleanup
journey.during: The operator kicks off a refinement run and monitors for out-of-scope plan proposals and unauthorized file changes
journey.after: Any out-of-scope attempt fails fast with a diagnostic terminal report, the worktree is reset, and the mutation lease is released

capability_breakdown.core_action: Persist and validate the authorized modification_scope against planned and actual file changes, raising a hard stop and cleaning the worktree on any violation
inputs: git diff --name-only changed_files from edd-do execution
starting revision and best accepted state for worktree reset
outputs: Progress record with resolved repo-relative modification_scope
Planning and validation results with distinct out-of-scope rejection reasons
OutOfScopeModificationError raised into the finalize path
Restored worktree and released mutation lease
state_changes: EddPlanRunner may reject a plan before edd-do runs
validate_candidate may reject a candidate after edd-do runs
workflow.py raises and finalizes on out-of-scope instead of quietly returning

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The run persists and threads the authorized modification scope to every scope-checking activity so fresh and resumed runs behave identically
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given an EDD refinement input with an authorized modification scope When initialize_run executes Then the resolved repo-relative scope is stored in the progress record and is available to edd_plan and validate_candidate on fresh or resumed runs
acceptance_criteria.jtbd: Persist authorized scope for the life of the run

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A shared path-containment helper accepts a repo-relative candidate when it exactly matches a scope entry or is nested under a directory prefix, using path-aware containment and not naive string prefixing
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given a repo-relative candidate path and an authorized scope list containing files and directory prefixes When the helper checks containment Then exact matches and descendants of directory prefixes pass while sibling or partial-prefix paths fail
acceptance_criteria.jtbd: Check file paths against authorized scope

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A plan that proposes files outside the authorized scope is rejected before edd-do runs and produces a diagnostic report
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given an EDD refinement plan that includes intended files outside the authorized scope When the plan is validated Then edd-do is skipped and a plan-time out-of-scope result is produced with the offending action, rationale, evidence, and paths

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Any file that actually changed outside the authorized scope is detected after edd-do and distinguished from a plan-time violation
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given an executed candidate with changed files outside the authorized scope When validate_candidate runs Then a diff_out_of_scope rejection is produced naming the offending path(s)
acceptance_criteria.jtbd: Detect unauthorized files in the actual diff

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A confirmed out-of-scope detection halts the run, reverts uncommitted changes, and records a distinct terminal reason
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given a plan-time or diff-time out-of-scope detection When workflow.py handles it Then it triggers the existing exception-driven finalize path, restores the worktree, writes the terminal report, and releases the mutation lease
acceptance_criteria.jtbd: Halt the run on scope violation

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A run that ends before any candidate is accepted leaves the worktree reset to the starting revision
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given a run ends before any candidate has been accepted When finalize_run executes Then the worktree is reset to the starting revision and no stray uncommitted changes remain
acceptance_criteria.jtbd: Leave a clean worktree after any stop

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A fully in-scope run continues through validation without a false scope alarm
acceptance_criteria.gherkin: Given an EDD refinement input with an authorized modification scope and a candidate whose intended and changed files are both within that scope When the workflow validates the candidate Then the candidate is accepted or proceeds normally without a scope rejection
acceptance_criteria.jtbd: Preserve normal behavior for authorized changes

edge_cases.gherkin: Given an EddRefinementInput with an empty or missing modification_scope When initialize_run executes Then the scope is persisted as an empty list and all later file checks fail as out-of-scope

edge_cases.criterion: Scope list contains paths with special characters or non-POSIX separators
edge_cases.gherkin: Given a modification_scope containing backslashes, tilde, or unicode segments When it is resolved Then it is normalized to repo-relative POSIX paths before storage and comparison

edge_cases.criterion: Scope directory prefix incorrectly matched by sibling name sharing a substring
edge_cases.gherkin: Given a scope entry 'foo/' and a candidate 'foo-bar/x' When the containment helper runs Then it rejects the candidate because path 'foo-bar' is not nested under 'foo'

edge_cases.criterion: Scope entry is an exact file and the candidate is a file in the same directory
edge_cases.gherkin: Given a scope entry naming an exact file and a candidate naming a sibling file in the same directory When containment is checked Then the sibling file is rejected
edge_cases.jtbd: Treat exact file entries as non-recursive

edge_cases.criterion: Resumed run must use the persisted modification_scope, not the original input
edge_cases.gherkin: Given a resumed run with a progress record containing a resolved modification_scope When edd_plan or validate_candidate runs Then it uses the stored scope and not a freshly derived value from CLI input
edge_cases.jtbd: Keep scope consistent across run resumptions

edge_cases.criterion: Out-of-scope detection before any candidate is accepted
edge_cases.gherkin: Given a plan-time out-of-scope detection with no best_accepted_state When the workflow finalizes Then it still resets the worktree to the starting_revision
edge_cases.jtbd: Clean worktree on early out-of-scope stop

edge_cases.criterion: Git worktree reset fails during finalize
edge_cases.gherkin: Given an out-of-scope stop where git reset --hard fails When finalize_run runs Then the terminal report still records out_of_scope_modification and the lease is released
edge_cases.jtbd: Preserve terminal reporting even if cleanup fails

questions.question: Should a confirmed out-of-scope stop count toward consecutive_confirmed_regressions or any existing budget counter, or is it always an immediate, separate terminal state?
Do we want a dedicated scope_violations list in the progress record / terminal report for observability, or is a single terminal report entry sufficient?
For the Requirement 3 pre-check: should a plan-time scope violation still get recorded as a candidate for get_candidate_status symmetry, even though no edd_do/validate_candidate ran?
Should trailing-slash normalization for directory scope entries be enforced at EddRefinementInput parse time or handled defensively in the containment helper?
Should this work be delivered as two vertical slices (scope persistence + plan-time rejection, then do-time validation + cleanup) or as one cohesive multi-activity change?

domain_knowledge: EDD refinement run lifecycle and authorized scope semantics
technical_knowledge: Git worktree reset and git diff mechanics
stakeholder_questions: Does out-of-scope stop count toward regression budget?
What telemetry fields are required for scope violations?
Should a plan-time violation still be reported as a candidate?
